source.label: Shown Space · preserved 2026 regular-season throws

metricDefinitions.label: Hypothetical route ranking
metricDefinitions.definition: Routes rank by the product of smoothed thrower delivery rates and receiver catch rates in compatible field zones. These are model-implied probabilities for screening, not calibrated forecasts.

filters: One to four passes, forward zone progression, with no repeated player.
Primary shortlist: at least 20 thrower attempts and 10 receiver targets on each zone transition, each across at least three games.
caveats: Exploratory in-sample screening, not a calibrated forecast or a claim of a global tactical optimum.
Broad spatial zones do not fix exact throw distance, marking pressure, weather, receiver separation, or timing.
Adjacent-zone historical throws often cross only part of a band; linking zone averages can overstate spatial progress. No exact continuous field path is estimated.
Thrower delivery and receiver catching are factored independently; fit together only in this hypothetical model.
Receiver exposure excludes untargeted throwaways; off-disc creation and ability to get open are not measured.
One regular-season game lacks throw data; playoffs excluded.
The five scores differ by only 0.062 percentage points; their numerical ordering is not a meaningful separation.
The displayed 90% intervals cover conditional Beta sampling uncertainty only, not model error, selection bias, or cross-team chemistry.
All three attacking end-zone boxes are pooled to support more stable estimates.

evidenceFlow.title: Input selection
evidenceFlow.detail: Read the same source-manifest files used by the explorer. Verified every file hash and reconciled throw IDs and aEC values with the reviewed snapshot.

evidenceFlow.title: Role model
evidenceFlow.detail: A throw is delivered if complete or dropped. Catching is measured among completions and recorded drops. Each player/transition rate receives 40 prior pseudo-observations at the corresponding league transition rate. Route scores multiply the four pairs of rates.

evidenceFlow.title: Search and sensitivity
evidenceFlow.detail: The primary search produced 1,749 eligible finished routes. The first candidate stayed first when prior strength changed to 20 or 80. Lowering the role sample floors to three produced 1,121,099 routes and admitted one-pass and two-pass alternatives; the highest-scoring shape still used four central passes, but Jacob Louie replaced Nico Ranabhat in that sparse-data search.

evidenceFlow.title: Route consistency
evidenceFlow.detail: Checked all five named sequences: each receiver becomes the next thrower, there are no repeated players, all transitions progress forward, and the stated sample/game floors hold.

items.title: Why raw total aEC does not identify an ideal scoring possession

source.label: Shown Space · About

metricDefinitions.label: aEC
metricDefinitions.definition: Shown Space defines adjusted Expected Contribution as normalized contribution so a drive totals one.

caveats: Stored throw values do not sum to exactly one on every scoring possession. Thrower and receiver credit on a completion refer to the same pass; adding them counts that event twice.

queries.summary: The normalization changes the optimization target: compare scoring reliability from a common starting state instead of adding seasonal box-leader totals.

source.label: Shown Space · possession audit

metricDefinitions.label: Scoring possession aEC
metricDefinitions.definition: Sum event aEC once per ordered possession ending in a recorded goal (event type 19), excluding nonconsecutive sequences and missing aEC.

caveats: This audit uses the cached season snapshot and the provider’s possession keys; it does not refresh the data.
